newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan crops advance on hot, dry weather.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan crops advance on hot, dry weather.

text.p: Hot, dry weather kept Saskatchewan's crop development ahead of the five-year 1992/96 average but began to threaten yield potential, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its crop report.

Eighty two percent of spring cereals were at or past the heading stage compared to the average 62 percent. Eleven percent of flax reached the boll stage compared with the average of two percent. Twenty eight percent of canola was at the podding stage compared to the average of 10 percent. Pulse crops were 33 percent podding compared to 10 percent last week and 26 percent of fall cereals were ripe versus two percent.
Drought and heat stress were the most commonly reported forms of crop damage. Wheat midge continued to be the primary insect concern.
The driest area extends from Kindersley to Lloydminster to Humboldt another dry area was from Saskatoon to Prince Albert.

An average 12 mm (0.4 inch) of rain fell on the southern grainbelt with up to 20 mm (0.9 inch) near Assiniboia. Hot, dry weather gave way to rain at the end of the week. Top soil moisture were rated slightly lower in the past week. There were several reports of farmers ploughing canola crops down and reseeding to oats for forage.

Central Saskatchewan reported an average of 8 mm (0.3 inch) of rain, but the Watrous area saw 14 mm (0.6 inch). Top soil moisture conditions deteriorated across the central grain belt as drought stress caused crop damage in many areas.
Northern districts saw an average 6 mm (0.2 inch) of rain with a high of 12 mm (0.5 inch). Drought and heat damage was reported in many areas. Topsoil moisture deteriorated in the past week.
